### Ten conclusions according to my own opinion on the doctrine of Albucaten Avena, who is called the author of the *Book of Causes*. <note>Pico attributes the "Liber de Causis" (a famous Neoplatonic text) to "Albucaten Avena," likely a corruption of the name of the Arabic philosopher Ibn al-Haytham or Avempace. Modern scholars know the book was actually based on Proclus.</note>

1. When Albucaten Avena said the soul is "above time," it must be understood as the soul being absolute in its substance, setting aside every operation that belongs to it insofar as it functions as a soul.
2. When Albucaten says every noble soul has three operations—divine, intellectual, and animal—it should be understood as follows: it has the first through an image of proportionality, the second through the formality of participation, and the third through the property of essentiality.
3. When Albucaten said that every primary cause has a "greater influence," you should understand "greater" to mean the excellence of its way of causing, and the intimacy of that which is produced within the thing.
4. Although Albucaten says that "Being," which is the first created thing, is "above intelligence," do not believe that it is distinct from intelligence according to its hypostasis <note>term: "hypostasis" — the underlying reality or individual substance of a thing.</note>.
5. When Albucaten said the First Cause is "beyond all description," this is true not so much because of what he first states—that it has no cause before it—but because of what he suggests secondarily: that it precedes every intelligible thing in a unified way.
6. What Albucaten says—that intelligence is a substance that cannot be divided—is most true because of the indistinct interpenetration of intelligible things within it.
7. From the preceding conclusion, one can understand how to interpret Albucaten’s saying that "every intelligence is full of forms."
8. Through the last proposition of Albucaten, we can understand the meaning of that division made by Plato at the beginning of the *Timaeus* <note>Plato’s dialogue on the creation of the universe.</note>; we can know that the soul is only included in that division by way of an extreme combination.
9. From the third-to-last proposition of Albucaten, it can be gathered that to decline more toward the senses than the intellect is not the nature of the soul as soul, but as it is "falling."
10. When Albucaten says that intelligence rules things "insofar as it is divine," it should be understood as a stabilizing rule, not an ordering one, which belongs to it insofar as it is intelligence.

---

### Eighty-five conclusions on mathematics according to my own opinion.

1. Mathematical sciences are not true sciences. <note>Pico argues here that mathematics deals with abstractions rather than the ultimate essence of reality.</note>
2. If happiness consists in the perfection of contemplation, mathematics does not contribute to happiness.
3. Mathematical sciences are not to be sought for their own sake, but as a path to other sciences.
4. Just as the subjects of mathematicians, if taken absolutely, do nothing to perfect the intellect, so too, if they are taken as images of higher things, they lead us directly by the hand to the contemplation of intelligible things.
5. Aristotle's saying about the ancients—that they erred in physical contemplation because they

<column-break/>

treated physical things mathematically—would be true if they had taken mathematics materially and not formally. Likewise, it is most true that the "moderns" who argue about natural things mathematically are destroying the foundations of natural philosophy.
6. Nothing is more harmful to a theologian than frequent and assiduous exercise in the mathematics of Euclid.
7. Just as medicine moves the spirits primarily as they rule the body, so music moves the spirits as they serve the soul.
8. Medicine heals the soul through the body, but music heals the body through the soul.
9. Through arithmetic—not the material kind, but the formal kind—one finds the best path to "natural prophecy."
10. Joachim, in his prophecies, proceeded by no other way than through formal numbers. <note>Refers to Joachim of Fiore, a medieval mystic who used complex numerical patterns in the Bible to predict historical eras.</note>
11. Through numbers, there is a way to investigate and understand everything knowable; to verify this conclusion, I promise to answer the eighty-three questions written below by way of numbers.

### Questions to which he promises to respond through numbers.

1. Whether God exists.
2. Whether He is infinite.
3. Whether He is the cause of all things.
4. Whether He is most simple. <note>In philosophy, "simple" means not composed of parts.</note>
5. Whether He is intelligent.
6. How God understands.
7. Whether there is a nature superior to the intellectual nature.
8. Whether the "quidditative being" <note>The "whatness" or essence of a thing.</note> of a thing is the most intimate being that a thing possesses.
9. What can be predicated of "humanity" in its most precise abstraction, and what cannot.
10. How the elements exist in the heavens.
11. What method should be held in the investigation of every knowable thing.
12. Whether above the nature of corporal things there is an incorporeal rational nature.
13. Whether above the rational nature there is an intellectual nature.
14. Whether there is any middle nature between the rational and intellectual natures.
15. Whether there is any middle nature between the intellectual nature and God.
16. Whether contradictories are compatible in any nature.
17. Whether contradictories coincide in any nature.
18. What number of years is naturally owed to the life of a good man and a bad man.
19. What number of years is naturally owed to the life of a human.
20. How many are the principal grades of the natures of the universe.
21. Whether a corporeal nature, as such, is active or only passive.
22. What "body" signifies.
23. Whether there are "unending dimensions" in matter.
24. Whether it is better for God to cause things than not to cause them.
25. Whether the creation of things externally proceeds necessarily from the divine essence hypostasized in three persons.
26. Whether something must necessarily mediate between the cause and the effect.
27. Whether...

->[CONCLUSIONS]<-

### *Twenty-six Magical Conclusions according to my own opinion.*

1. All Magic practiced among the Moderns, which the Church rightly exterminates, has no firmness, no foundation, and no truth, because it depends on the hands of the enemies of the first truth—those powers of darkness which pour the darkness of falsehood into poorly disposed intellects. <note>Pico is distinguishing between "black magic" or demonology (which he rejects) and his own "Natural Magic."</note>
2. Natural Magic is lawful and not prohibited, and regarding the universal theoretical foundations of this science, I set down the following conclusions according to my own opinion.
3. Magic is the practical part of natural science.
4. From this conclusion and the paradoxical conclusion number 47, it follows that Magic is the noblest part of natural science.
5. There is no virtue in heaven or on earth, existing seminally or separately, which the magus cannot actuate and unite. <note>original: "seminaliter." Pico refers to "seminal reasons," the hidden potential or "seeds" within nature that a practitioner can bring to fruition.</note>
6. Whatever wonderful work is done, whether it be magical, cabalistic, or of any other kind, it must be referred principally to God, the glorious and blessed, whose grace daily rains down the super-celestial waters of miraculous virtues upon contemplative men of good will.
7. The works of Christ could not have been done either by way of Magic or by way of Kabbalah. <note>Pico was often accused of suggesting Christ was a magician; here he explicitly denies it to protect his orthodoxy.</note>
8. The miracles of Christ are the most certain argument of his divinity, not because of the thing done, but because of his manner of doing it.
9. There is no science that makes us more certain of the divinity of Christ than Magic and Kabbalah. <note>This was Pico’s most dangerous claim: that esoteric Jewish and "Natural" sciences prove Christian dogma better than standard theology.</note>
10. What a Magus as a human does through art, nature does naturally by making a human.
11. The wonders of the Magical art are not performed except through the union and actuation of those things which are seminally and separately in nature.
12. The form of all Magical power comes from the soul of man standing, and not falling. <note>Refers to the state of the soul being "upright" or intellectually active rather than "fallen" or distracted by the senses.</note>
13. To practice Magic is nothing other than to marry the world. <note>original: "maritare mundum." This is one of Pico's most famous phrases, suggesting the Magus unites the passive powers of earth with the active influences of heaven.</note>
14. If there is any nature immediately close to us, which is either simply or at least largely rational, it possesses Magic in the highest degree, and through participation in it, Magic can be more perfect in men.
15. No Magical operation can have any efficacy unless it has an annexed work of <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>The Jewish mystical tradition involving the interpretation of scripture and names of God.</note>, whether explicit or implicit.
16. That nature which is the <term>Horizon</term> <note>original: "Orizon." A technical term in Neoplatonism for the human soul, which stands on the "horizon" between the temporal world and the eternal world.</note> of eternal time is closest to the Magus, but below him.
17. Magic is proper to that nature which is the Horizon of time and eternity; it must be sought from there through the proper methods known to the wise.
18. That nature which is the Horizon of temporal eternity is closest to the Magus, but above him, and Kabbalah is proper to it.
19. Voices and words have efficacy in a Magical work for this reason: because that in which nature first exercises Magic is the voice of God.
20. Every voice has power in Magic, insofar as it is formed by the voice of God.
21. Non-meaningful voices have more power in Magic 

<column-break/>

than meaningful ones; he who is profound can understand the reason for this conclusion from the preceding one. <note>Pico refers to "barbarous names" or ritual sounds that bypass the rational mind to act directly on the fabric of reality.</note>
22. No names, insofar as they are meaningful and as they are named, taken individually and by themselves, can have power in a Magical work, unless they are Hebrew, or derived closely from them.
23. Every number except for three and ten are material in Magic; these two are formal, and in Magical Arithmetic, they are the numbers of numbers.
24. From the principles of the more secret philosophy, it is necessary to confess that characters and figures have more power in a Magical work than any material quality could.
25. Just as characters are proper to a Magical work, so numbers are proper to a work of Kabbalah, with a middle ground existing between both, appropriated through the use of letters.
26. Just as something is made through the special and immediate influx of the first agent that is not attained through the mediation of causes, so through the work of Kabbalah—if it is pure and immediate Kabbalah—something is made which no Magic can reach.

### *Thirty-one conclusions according to my own opinion on the manner of understanding the hymns of Orpheus according to Magic, that is, the secret wisdom of divine and natural things first discovered by me in them.*

1. Just as it is not permitted to explain in public the secret Magic first elicited by us from the hymns of <term>Orpheus</term> <note>A legendary Greek hero and musician. Pico believed the "Orphic Hymns" contained hidden theological truths similar to the Hebrew Kabbalah.</note>, so it will be useful to demonstrate it through the headings of aphorisms—as will be done in the conclusions written below—to excite the minds of contemplative men.
2. Nothing is more efficacious than the hymns of Orpheus in natural Magic, if the proper music, intention of the soul, and other circumstances known to the wise are applied.
3. The names of the gods of whom Orpheus sings are not the names of deceiving demons, from whom evil and not good proceeds, but are the names of natural and divine virtues, distributed to the world by the true God for the greatest utility of man, if he knows how to use them.
4. Just as the hymns of David wonderfully serve the work of Kabbalah, so the hymns of Orpheus serve the work of truly lawful and natural Magic.
5. The number of the hymns of Orpheus is the same as the number with which the triple God created the age, numbered under the form of the <term>Pythagorean quaternary</term> <note>The "Tetractys," a triangular figure of ten points, symbolizing the organizational pattern of the universe.</note>.
6. For whatever natural or divine virtues there are, the analogical property is the same; likewise the name is the same, the hymn the same, and the work the same, provided proportion is maintained; and he who attempts to explain them will see the correspondence.
7. He who does not know how to perfectly intellectualize sensible properties through the way of secret analogy will understand nothing sound from the hymns of Orpheus.
8. He who profoundly and intellectually understands the division of the Unity of Venus into a trinity of Graces, and the Unity of Fate into a trinity of Fates, and the Unity of Saturn into a trinity of Jupiter, Neptune, and Pluto, will see the proper mode of proceeding in Orphic theology.

9. The **Curetes** <note>In Greek mythology, these were armored dancers who protected the infant Zeus; Pico identifies them here with angelic powers.</note> in the works of Orpheus are the same as the **Powers** in the works of Dionysius. <note>Dionysius the Areopagite, a Christian mystic who categorized the hierarchy of angels.</note>
10. Whoever attempts the work of the preceding conclusion should employ the work of **Kabbalah** according to that which is attributed to the **Fear of Isaac**. <note>"Fear of Isaac" (Pachad Yitzchak) is a traditional name for the Sephirah of Gevurah, representing judgment and power.</note>
11. In vain will one approach **Palaemon** and **Leucothea** <note>Sea deities in Greek myth.</note> if they have not first drawn in **Nereus**, nor will they draw in Nereus if they have not operated around the primary **animal trinity**.
12. Through the number **eight** of the hymns of the sea, the property of our **bodily nature** is designated.
13. **Typhon** in Orpheus is the same as **Samael** in the Kabbalah. <note>Typhon was a monstrous giant in Greek myth; Samael is an adversarial figure or angel of death in Jewish tradition.</note>
14. If anyone operates intellectually in the work of the preceding conclusion, they will bind the **North** by means of the **South**; but if they operate entirely in a worldly manner, they will bring **judgment** upon themselves.
15. **Night** in Orpheus is the same as **En Sof** in the Kabbalah. <note>original: "Ensoph." En Sof refers to the Infinite, the unknowable Godhead in Jewish mysticism before any emanation.</note>
16. From the preceding conclusion, one can explain more correctly than **Proclus** <note>A late Neoplatonist philosopher who commented extensively on Orpheus.</note> what that saying of the Theologian <note>Orpheus was often called "The Theologian" in these circles.</note> means when he introduces the **Maker of the world** consulting **Night** about the creation of the world.
17. From these same sayings, it can be understood why in the *Symposium* <note>Plato’s dialogue on love.</note> **Poros** (the son of Counsel) is named by **Diotima**, and why in Holy Scripture **Jesus** is called the **Angel of Great Counsel**.
18. As the **watery soul** generates lower things, contemplates higher things, and rests within itself, it is sung of by Orpheus in a triple hymn: of the **Sea**, of **Neptune**, and of the **Ocean**.
19. One who has not drawn in **Vesta** <note>Hestia, goddess of the hearth and stability.</note> will have nothing firm in their work.
20. Through the number **seven** of the hymns attributed to the **Paternal Mind**—namely those of **Protogonos**, **Pallas**, **Saturn**, the race of **Rhea**, the law of **Bacchus**—an intelligent and profound contemplator can conjecture something regarding the **consummation of the age**. <note>The end of the world.</note>
21. The work of the preceding hymns is nothing without the work of **Kabbalah**, whose property it is to put into practice every **formal quantity**, both continuous and discrete.
22. One who does not divide **Heroes** into two types—those who are **native** and those who are **adventitious**—will often err.
23. One who approaches **Apollo** will mediate the work through **Bacchus of the Three-Year Festival** and will complete it through the **Ineffable Name**.
24. One will not be intoxicated by any **Bacchus** who has not first been coupled with his own **Muse**.
25. Through the number **four** of the hymns attributed to the **primary worldly form**, the nature of its own "formable" essence is designated for us.
26. One who has perfectly returned into the **soul** will have made their own form equal to the **primary form**.
27. One who attempts the work of the preceding conclusion will approach the **third Jove** <note>Jupiter/Zeus.</note> as one who is **living**, not as one who is **vivifying** (giving life).
28. In vain does one approach **Nature** and **Proteus** if they have not drawn in **Pan**.
29. Just as there is a **particular animation** after a **universal animation**, so there is a **particular providence** after a **universal providence**.
30. From the preceding conclusion, it can be known why **Ovid**, in his curse-poem *The Ibis*, after invoking the name that rules the earth and water, then invokes the **Earth** and **Neptune**.
31. One who carefully notes what was said by **Aristotle** in his explanation of the definition of the **soul** will see why Orpheus attributed **vigilance** to **Pallas** and **Veneris** (Venus).

->Eighty-one Cabalistic Conclusions according to my own opinion, derived from the very foundations of the Hebrew sages, which most strongly confirm the Christian religion.<-

1. Whatever other Kabbalists may say, I would distinguish the science of Kabbalah by a primary division into the science of the **Sephirot** <note>The ten emanations of God.</note> and the science of **Semor**, <note>Likely referring to "Shemot" or Names, the study of divine names.</note> as if into **practical** and **speculative** parts.
2. Whatever other Kabbalists may say, I would divide the **speculative** part of Kabbalah into four parts, corresponding to the fourfold division of philosophy that I am accustomed to asserting. The first is the science of **Alphabetic Revolution**, corresponding to the part of philosophy I call **universal philosophy**. The second, third, and fourth parts are the threefold **Merchiana**, <note>Referring to the "Merkavah" or Chariot of Ezekiel; mystical accounts of the divine realm.</note> corresponding to the threefold division of particular philosophy: concerning **divine**, **intermediate**, and **sensible** natures.
3. The science which is the **practical** part of Kabbalah puts into practice all **formal metaphysics** and **lower theology**.
4. **En Sof** <note>original: "Ensoph."</note> is not to be numbered among the other numerations (Sephirot), because it is the **abstract and communicated unity** of those numerations, not a coordinated unity.
5. Every Hebrew Kabbalist, according to the principles and sayings of the science of Kabbalah, is inevitably forced to concede regarding the **Trinity** and each divine person—**Father, Son, and Holy Spirit**—precisely that which the **Catholic faith of Christians** posits, without addition, subtraction, or variation.
**Corollary:** Not only those who deny the Trinity, but also those who posit it in another way than the Catholic Church does—such as the **Arians** and **Sabellians** <note>Early Christian sects deemed heretical for their views on the nature of the Trinity.</note>—can be clearly refuted if the principles of Kabbalah are admitted.
6. The **three great names of God** consisting of four letters, <note>Variations of the Tetragrammaton.</note> which are found in the secrets of the Kabbalists, must be attributed through a wondrous appropriation to the three persons of the Trinity in this way: the name <note>blank space in original</note> is the **Father’s**, the name <note>blank space in original</note> is the **Son’s**, and the name <note>blank space in original</note> is the **Holy Spirit’s**—as can be understood by one who is deep in the science of Kabbalah.
7. No Hebrew Kabbalist can deny that the name **Jesus**, if we interpret it according to the method and principles of Kabbalah, signifies precisely all of this and nothing else: that is, **God the Son of God**, and the **Wisdom of the Father**, united to **human nature** in the unity of a person through the **third person of the Divinity**, who is the most burning fire of love.
8. From the preceding conclusion, it can be understood why **Paul** said that the name of **Jesus** was given, which is **above every name**, and why it is said that at the name of Jesus **every knee should bow**—of things in heaven, on earth, and under the earth—which is also highly Cabalistic, and can be understood by one who is deep in Kabbalah.
9. If there is any human conjecture concerning the **last times**, we can investigate through the most secret path of Kabbalah that the **consummation of the age** will occur **five hundred and fourteen years and twenty-five days** from now.
10. That which is called <note>blank space in original</note> among the Kabbalists is undoubtedly that which is named **Pallas** by Orpheus, the **Paternal Mind** by Zoroaster, the **Son of God** by Hermes (Mercury), **Wisdom** by Pythagoras, and the **Intelligible Sphere** by Parmenides.

### C O N C L U S I O N S

11. The manner by which rational souls are sacrificed to God through the archangel <note>Likely referring to Metatron, often identified in Kabbalah as the celestial high priest who offers the souls of the righteous.</note> is only through the separation of the soul from the body—not the body from the soul except by accident, as happens in the **death of the kiss**, of which it is written: *Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy ones.* <note>original: "pretiosa in conspectu domini mors fanctorum eius." The "death of the kiss" refers to a mystical state of ecstasy so intense that the soul leaves the body to unite with God.</note>

12. No one can operate through pure **Kabbalah** who is not rationally intellectual.

13. He who operates in Kabbalah without the mixture of anything foreign, if he remains long in the work, will die from **the kiss**; <note>original: "Binfica," a Latinized form of the Hebrew *binshika*, meaning "with a kiss."</note> and if he errs in the work or approaches it without being purified, he will be devoured by **Azazel** through the property of judgment. <note>In Kabbalah, Azazel represents the forces of severity or "the left side" that can consume those who are spiritually unprepared.</note>

14. Through the letter **Shin**, <note>original: "Scin."</note> which mediates in the name of **Jesus**, it is signified to us Kabbalistically that the world then rested perfectly as if in its own perfection, when the **Yod** was joined with the **Vav**; <note>Yod and Vav are letters of the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God). Pico argued that inserting "Shin" into the middle of the divine name (YHWH) produced the name of Jesus (YHSWH), making the name pronounceable and bringing God into the human realm.</note> this was accomplished in **Christ**, who was the true Son of God and man.

15. Through the name **Yod, He, Vav, He**, <note>The Tetragrammaton, the ineffable name of God.</note> which is the name the Kabbalists say will be the name of the **Messiah**, it is clearly recognized that he will be God, the Son of God, made man through the Holy Spirit, and that after him, for the perfection of the human race, the **Paraclete** <note>The Holy Spirit as "Comforter" or "Advocate."</note> will descend upon men.

16. From the mystery of the three letters that are in the word **Shabbat**, that is <term>שבת</term> <note>The Hebrew word for Sabbath.</note> we can interpret Kabbalistically that the world "sabbathizes" (rests) when the Son of God becomes man, and finally, the future Sabbath will occur when men are regenerated into the Son of God.

17. Whoever knows what the **purest wine** is among the Kabbalists will know why David said, *I shall be inebriated by the abundance of your house*, <note>original: "inebriabor ab ubertate domus tuæ."</note> and what kind of drunkenness the ancient poet **Musaeus** said was happiness, and what so many **Bacchuses** signify in the works of **Orpheus**. <note>Pico is synthesizing Jewish mysticism with Greek mythology, suggesting that "divine intoxication" is a universal metaphor for spiritual union with God.</note>

18. Whoever joins **Astrology** to **Kabbalah** will see that it is more fitting to "sabbathize" and rest after Christ on the **Lord’s day** (Sunday) than on the day of the **Sabbath** (Saturday).

19. If we explain Kabbalistically that saying of the prophet, *They sold the righteous for silver*, <note>original: "Vendiderunt iustum argento" (Amos 2:6).</note> it signifies nothing else to us than this: namely, that God the Redeemer was sold for silver.

20. If the Kabbalists turn their attention to their interpretation of this word <term>אז</term>, <note>Hebrew *Az*, meaning "then."</note> which signifies "then," they will be greatly enlightened regarding the mystery of the **Trinity**.

21. Whoever joins the saying of the Kabbalists—who say that the numeration <note>Refers to a *Sefirah*, one of the ten attributes of God.</note> called **"the Righteous"** and **"the Redeemer"** is also called **Ze** <note>Hebrew *Ze* (זה), meaning "this."</note>—with the saying of the **Talmudists**, who say that **Isaac** went like **Ze** carrying his own cross, <note>Isaac carrying the wood for his sacrifice is a traditional Christian "type" or foreshadowing of Christ carrying the cross.</note> will see that what was prefigured in Isaac was fulfilled in Christ, who was the true God sold for silver.

22. Through the sayings of the Kabbalists regarding the **redness of Esau**, and that saying found in the book **Genesis Rabbah** <note>original: "Brefit Rhaba," a classic collection of Jewish homilies on the Book of Genesis.</note> that "Esau was red, and a red one will avenge him," <note>original: "Esau fuit rubeus, & rubeus eum vlciscetur."</note> concerning whom it is said, *Why is your garment red?*, it is expressly held that Christ (concerning whom our doctors explain the same text) will be the one who takes vengeance upon the unclean powers.

23. Through that saying of **Jeremiah**, *He has lacerated His word*, <note>original: "lacerauit verbum suū." A mystical reading of Lamentations 2:17.</note> according to the explanation of the Kabbalists, we are to understand that God lacerated the holy and blessed God for the sake of sinners.

24. Through the response of the Kabbalists to the question of why, in the Book of Numbers, the portion <note>original: "particula," referring to a section of the Torah.</note> regarding the **death of Miriam** is joined to the portion regarding the **Red Heifer**, and through their explanation of that passage where **Moses**, regarding the sin of the golden calf, said, *Blot me out*, <note>original: "dele me" (Exodus 32:32).</note> and through the sayings in the **Book of Zohar** <note>original: "libro Zoar."</note> on the text, *And by his bruises we are healed*, <note>original: "Et eius liuore sanati sumus" (Isaiah 53:5).</note> the Jews—who say it was not fitting for the death of Christ to satisfy for the sins of the human race—are inevitably refuted.

<column-break/>

25. Every Kabbalist must concede that the **Messiah** was to deliver them from diabolical, and not merely temporal, captivity.

26. Every Kabbalist must concede, from the sayings of the teachers of this science who state this manifest truth, that **original sin** will be expiated at the coming of the Messiah.

27. From the principles of the Kabbalists, it is evidently drawn out that through the coming of the Messiah, the necessity of **circumcision** shall be removed.

28. Through the word <term>את</term>, <note>Hebrew *Et*, an untranslatable particle often used to mark the direct object. Pico reads it as a mystery because it consists of the first and last letters of the Hebrew alphabet (Aleph and Tav), similar to "Alpha and Omega."</note> which is placed twice in that text, *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth*, I believe Moses signified the creation of the **intellectual nature** and the **animal nature**, which in the natural order preceded the creation of heaven and earth.

29. What is said by the Kabbalists—that a **"green line"** <note>The *Kav ha-Yarok*, which in Kabbalah is said to surround the world and from which darkness emanates.</note> circles the universe—is most fittingly said regarding the final conclusion which we stated from the mind of **Porphyry**. <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher.</note>

30. The Kabbalists must necessarily concede, according to their own principles, that the true Messiah is to be such that it may truly be said of him: He is **God and the Son of God**.

31. When you hear the Kabbalists place **informity** <note>A state of being without form; potentiality.</note> in **Repentance**, <note>original: "Thesua," likely *Teshuvah*. Pico links the concept of returning to God with a return to a state of primal, unformed potential.</note> understand it as informity by accident to formality, not by privation.

32. If we join the double **Aleph** <note>original: "א"</note> found in the text, *The scepter shall not be removed etc.*, to the double Aleph in the text, *God possessed me from the beginning*, and the double Aleph in the text, *But the earth was void*, we shall understand through the way of Kabbalah that **Jacob** was there speaking of that true Messiah, who was **Jesus of Nazareth**.

33. Through this word which is written with **Aleph, Yod, and Shin** <note>The Hebrew word *Ish* (איש), meaning "man."</note> (and signifies "Man"), which is attributed to God when He is called a **"Man of War,"** we are most perfectly reminded of the mystery of the **Trinity** through the way of Kabbalah.

34. Through the name written with three letters—**He, Vav, and Aleph** <note>The Hebrew word *Hu* (הוא), meaning "He."</note>—which is most properly attributed to God, and most conveniently aligns not only with the Kabbalists (who say this expressly and often) but also with the theology of **Dionysius the Areopagite**, the mystery of the Trinity along with the possibility of the **Incarnation** is declared to us through the way of Kabbalah.

35. If God is understood in Himself as the **Infinite**, as the **One**, and according to Himself, we understand nothing as proceeding from Him; rather, we understand a separation from all things, a total closure of Himself within Himself, and an extreme, deep, and solitary retraction into the most remote recess of His divinity—He being most inwardly contained within the abyss of His own darkness, and in no way manifesting Himself in the expansion and profusion of His goodness and fount-like splendor.

36. From the preceding conclusion, it can be understood why it is said among the Kabbalists that God **clothed Himself in ten garments** when He created the world. <note>Refers to the ten *Sefirot*, the emanations through which the Infinite God interacts with the finite world.</note>

# GIOVANNI PICO DELLA MIRANDOLA

37. He who understands, within the right-hand coordination, the subordination of piety to wisdom, will perfectly understand through the way of **Kabbalah** how Abraham, in his own day, saw the day of Christ through a straight line and rejoiced. <note>Refers to John 8:56. In Kabbalah, the "right-hand" side is associated with the emanation of Mercy (Chesed), which Pico connects to Abraham.</note>

38. The effects that followed after the death of Christ ought to convince any **Kabbalist** that Jesus the Nazarene was the true Messiah.

39. From this conclusion and the thirtieth one placed above, it follows that any **Kabbalist** must concede that when Jesus was asked who he was, he responded most correctly saying, "I am the beginning who speaks to you." <note>original: "ego sum principium qui loquor vobis." A Latin rendering of John 8:25.</note>

40. **Kabbalists** must inevitably concede this: that the true Messiah will purify men through water.

41. It can be known in **Kabbalah** through the mystery of the "closed Mem" why Christ sent the **Paraclete** after him. <note>The "closed Mem" is a Hebrew letter form (ם) appearing strangely in the middle of a word in Isaiah 9:7, often interpreted by mystical commentators as a sign of a hidden or virgin birth. The Paraclete refers to the Holy Spirit.</note>

42. It is known through the foundations of **Kabbalah** that Jesus spoke rightly: "Before Abraham was born, I am." <note>original: "Antequam nasceretur Abraam ego sum." From John 8:58.</note>

43. Through the mystery of the two letters **Vav** and **Yod**, it is known how the Messiah himself, as God, was the principle of himself as man. <note>Vav and Yod are components of the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God. Pico uses their symbolic values to bridge the divine and human natures of Christ.</note>

44. It is known from **Kabbalah**, through the mystery of the northern part, why God will judge the world by fire. <note>In Kabbalah, the North is associated with the emanation of Gevurah (Strength/Judgment), which is symbolized by fire.</note>

45. It is known most clearly in **Kabbalah** why the Son of God came with the water of baptism, and the Holy Spirit with fire.

46. Through the eclipse of the sun which happened at the death of Christ, it can be known according to the foundations of **Kabbalah** that the Son of God and the true Messiah suffered then.

47. He who knows the property of the North in **Kabbalah** will know why Satan promised the kingdoms of the world to Christ if he would fall down and worship him.

48. Whatever others may say, I say that the ten spheres correspond to the ten **numerations** in this way: starting from the "building," Jupiter belongs to the fourth, Mars to the fifth, the Sun to the sixth, Saturn to the seventh, Venus to the eighth, Mercury to the ninth, and the Moon to the tenth; then, above the "building," the firmament corresponds to the third, the *primum mobile* to the second, and the empyrean heaven to the first. <note>Pico is mapping the ten Sefirot—the "numerations" of divine energy—onto the physical structure of the cosmos according to medieval astronomy.</note>

49. He who knows the correspondence of the ten commandments to the prohibitions through the conjunction of **Astrological** truth with theological truth will see from our foundation of the preceding conclusion—whatever other **Kabbalists** may say—that the first commandment corresponds to the first numeration, the second to the second, the third to the third, the fourth to the seventh, the fifth to the fourth, the sixth to the fifth, the seventh to the ninth, the eighth to the eighth, the ninth to the sixth, and the tenth to the tenth.

50. When **Kabbalists** say that children are to be sought from the seventh and eighth, you should say that this is understood in the "lower **Merkavah**" such that one is asked to give, and the other not to prohibit; and he who is intelligent in **Astrology** and **Kabbalah** can understand from the preceding conclusions what it gives and what it prohibits. <note>The "Merkavah" or Chariot refers to the visionary tradition of the divine realm.</note>

51. Just as the Moon was full in Solomon, so the Sun was full in the true Messiah, who was Jesus; and regarding the correspondence to the waning in **Zedekiah**, one can conjecture if he dives deep into **Kabbalah**. <note>King Solomon represents the peak of the Davidic line, while Zedekiah represents its decline; Pico equates Christ with the ultimate "Solar" fulfillment of this cycle.</note>

52. From the preceding conclusion, it can be understood why the evangelist Matthew omitted certain names in those fourteen generations before Christ.

53. Since "light being made" is nothing other than participating in

<column-break/>

light, that exposition of the **Kabbalists** is very fitting: that in the phrase "let there be light," we understand the "shining mirror" through the light; and in the phrase "light was made," we understand the "non-shining mirror." <note>Pico distinguishes between the direct light of God (shining mirror) and the reflected or mediated light of creation (non-shining mirror).</note>

54. What the **Kabbalists** say—that we are to be made blessed in the "shining mirror" stored away for the saints in the world to come—is precisely the same thing, following their foundations, as what we say: that the saints are to be made blessed in the Son.

55. What the **Kabbalists** say—that the light stored in the sevenfold shines more than the light left behind—marvelously agrees with **Pythagorean** Arithmetic.

56. He who knows how to unfold the four (*quaternary*) into the ten (*denary*) will have a method, if he is skilled in **Kabbalah**, for deriving the name of seventy-two letters from the **Ineffable Name**. <note>Refers to the Tetractys and the "Shem HaMephorash," a 72-fold name of God derived from Exodus.</note>

57. Through the preceding conclusion, one intelligent in formal Arithmetic can understand that to operate through the **Shem HaMephorash** is a property of rational nature. <note>original: "Scemamphoras."</note>

58. It would be more correct to explain that term *Becadmin*—which the Chaldaic gloss places over the word **Bereshit**—as referring to the ideas of wisdom rather than the thirty-two paths as other **Kabbalists** say; nevertheless, both are correct in **Kabbalah**. <note>Bereshit is the first word of Genesis, "In the beginning." The Chaldaic gloss (Targum) often translates it as "In/By Wisdom" (Be-Hokhma).</note>

59. He who deeply considers the fourfold state of things—first of union and stability of dwelling, second of procession, third of reversion, fourth of beatific reunion—will see the letter **Beth** operate: with the first letter, the first state; with the middle, the medium; and with the last letters, the final state.

60. From the preceding conclusion, a contemplative man can understand why the Law of God begins with the letter **Beth**, of which it is written: that it is immaculate, that it was with him composing all things, that it converts souls, and that it makes one give fruit in its season.

61. Through the same conclusion, it can be known that the same Son, who is the wisdom of the Father, is the one who unites all things in the Father, and through whom all things were made, and by whom all things are converted, and in whom finally all things keep the Sabbath.

62. He who deeply considers the ninefold number of the beatitudes, of which Matthew speaks in the Gospel, will see that they marvelously agree with the ninefold set of the nine **numerations** which are below the first, which is the abyss of inaccessible divinity. <note>The first Sefirah (Keter/Crown) is often considered beyond human comprehension, leaving nine that relate to the created world and human virtue.</note>

63. Just as Aristotle himself concealed the more divine philosophy (which the ancient philosophers veiled under fables and stories) under the face of philosophical speculation and obscured it with brevity of words, so **Rabbi Moses the Egyptian**, in the book called by the Latins the "Guide for the Perplexed," while appearing to walk with the philosophers through the superficial rind of his words, encompasses the mysteries of **Kabbalah** through the hidden understandings of deep sense. <note>original: "Rabbi Moyses Aegyptius... dux neutrorum." This refers to Maimonides. Pico argues that even rationalist Jewish philosophers were secretly Kabbalists.</note>

64. In the text, "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one," it is more correct to understand there a collection from the lower to the higher, and from the higher to the lower, than a collection from the lower to the higher twice.

65. It is more correct that "Amen" signifies **Tipheret** and the Kingdom, as is shown by the way of number, than that it signifies the Kingdom alone, as some wish. <note>Tipheret (Beauty) and Malchut (Kingdom) are two of the Sefirot.</note>

66. I adapt our soul to the ten **Sefirot** in this way: that through its unity it is with the first, through intellect with the second, through reason with the third, through the higher concupiscible power with the fourth, through the... <note>The text cuts off mid-list, continuing Pico’s psychological mapping of the human soul onto the divine emanations.</note>

<summary>Pico presents a series of mystical propositions linking Kabbalistic principles (Sefirot and Hebrew letter symbolism) to Christian doctrines and the structure of the cosmos. He argues that Jewish mystics and even rationalist philosophers like Maimonides secretly held truths that confirm the divinity of Jesus.</summary>
<keywords>Kabbalah, Sefirot, Messiah, Maimonides, Astrology, Christianity, Neoplatonism, Shem HaMephorash, Sacred Geometry, Biblical Exegesis</keywords>

--- Page 374 ---
<meta>This page concludes the "Cabalistic Conclusions" of Giovanni Pico della Mirandola. The previous page established connections between Christian doctrine and Jewish mysticism, specifically linking the figure of Christ to the Sefirot (divine emanations). This final page completes the 900 propositions that Pico famously offered to defend in Rome in 1486, ending with a synthesis of astrology, mathematics, and mysticism, followed by the printer's colophon.</meta>

# CONCLUSIONS

...the higher <term>irascible power</term><note>The "irascible" is a traditional psychological term for the part of the soul associated with courage, anger, and the will to overcome obstacles.</note> with the fifth [dwelling], through free will with the sixth, and through all this—as it turns toward higher things—with the seventh, as it turns toward lower things with the eighth, and a mixture of both (rather through indifference or alternating adherence than through simultaneous containment) with the ninth, and through the power by which it inhabits the first dwelling with the tenth.

**67** Through the saying of the **Kabbalists** that the Heavens are made of fire and water, he manifests to us both the theological truth concerning the **Sefirot** <note>The ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> themselves and the philosophical truth: that the elements in heaven exist only according to their active virtue. <note>In Hebrew, the word for heaven, *shamayim*, is often mystically interpreted as a compound of *esh* (fire) and *mayim* (water).</note>

**68** He who understands what the "ten" is in formal arithmetic, and has known the nature of the first spherical number, will know that which I have not yet read in any **Kabbalist**: namely, that it is the foundation of the great secret of *Yohelei* <note>original: "Iohelei." This likely refers to a specific mystical name or permutation of the divine name used in Kabbalistic meditation.</note> in the **Kabbalah**.

<column-break/>

**69** From the foundation of the preceding conclusion, one can likewise know the secret of the fifty gates of understanding, and of the thousandth generation, and of the kingdom of all ages. <note>The "Fifty Gates of Understanding" (*Binah*) represent the levels of divine wisdom a human mind can achieve.</note>

**70** Through the method of reading without vowel points in the Law, the method of writing divine things and the unified containment through the indeterminate scope of divine things is shown to us. <note>Torah scrolls are written without vowels; Kabbalists believe this "unpointed" text allows for infinite layers of meaning to be extracted by varying the vocalization.</note>

**71** Through that which the **Kabbalists** say concerning Egypt, as attested by experience, we must believe that the land of Egypt exists in the analogy and subordination of the property of power.

**72** Just as true **astrology** teaches us to read in the book of God, so **Kabbalah** teaches us to read in the book of the Law.

## The End of the Nine Hundred Conclusions of Giovanni Pico della Mirandola.
